You are synthesizing a unified hypothesis from multiple parent hypotheses.
Goal: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from the limitation group 'Leakage-free generalisation protocol': L1, L2, L11, L20, L22, L27, L37, C2): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and with a simple supervised baseline trained on the same labelled images (L31) where relevant.
Parent hypotheses: Parent 1:
TITLE: Leave-one-out empirical-CDF normalisation for inductive MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Replace test-set min-max with each branch's (and level's) leave-one-out empirical CDF over support-normal patch scores; keep the 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
HYPOTHESIS: At K >= 4, LOO empirical-CDF normalisation keeps image and pixel AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, and its support-derived threshold gives realised specificity within 5 points of 95% on every held-out dataset, with a smaller miss than the percentile normaliser at K = 2.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; support percentiles as in the problem; support LOO empirical CDF). Reference set R_bl: patch scores of each support computed against a memory bank of the other K-1 supports (few-shot) or the text anchors (zero-shot). F_bl(s) = (rank of s in R_bl + 0.5)/(|R_bl| + 1); fused map = 0.5 F_zero + 0.5 F_few (averaged over levels as in MVFA); image score = max of fused map. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC; sensitivity at 95% specificity with tau = 95th percentile of LOO support image scores; realised specificity; per-image score shift under test-set resampling (exactly zero by construction for inductive variants).
RATIONALE: Percentiles use two points of the support distribution and are noisy for small K. Following ReCAP's non-parametric normal memory, each branch can instead be mapped through the full leave-one-out empirical CDF of support-normal patch scores, which places both branches on the same [0, 1] scale defined only by the K supports, before MVFA's unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
METHOD: 1) test_few.py: refactor into score_image(x, model, support_feats, refs) that uses no other test image; remove the test-set min-max block. 2) utils.py: build_refs(support_feats, text_feats): for i in 1..K, few-shot patch scores of support i against the bank of the others and zero-shot scores; store sorted arrays per branch and level. 3) cdf(s, R) via torch.searchsorted. 4) Fusion 0.5/0.5 and max pooling unchanged. Hyper-parameters: none beyond nominal specificity 95%; no training.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, ECE after a logistic map fitted on source validation. Falsified if AUROC drops by more than 1 point at K >= 4.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Empirical CDF of anatomy residuals for inductive MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Subtract a shrunk position-wise median of support scores from every patch score and map the residual through one global leave-one-out empirical CDF of support residuals, then fuse with MVFA's unchanged rule.
HYPOTHESIS: Mapping position-wise residuals through a global empirical CDF matches the global empirical CDF in image AUROC (within 1 point) and improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point on aligned modalities, with lower variance across support draws at K = 2 than the position-wise CDF.
RATIONALE: This combination takes the positional part from the position-wise parent only as a location correction, and the scale from the empirical-CDF parent as a single global reference. Separating location (local, needs few values) from scale (global, needs many) avoids estimating local spreads from a handful of supports, which is the weak point of both a position-wise z-score and a local CDF at K = 2.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: positional_median(support_maps) with 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage 20; residual reference set R = {s - med_j} over all LOO support patches. 2) test_few.py: r = s_j - med_j; F(r) via searchsorted on R; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: global empirical CDF; position-wise CDF. Metric of stability: standard deviation of AUROC over support draws. Falsified if residual CDF is not more stable than the position-wise CDF at K = 2.
